title: To be: I am 20 (¡no 'I have 20'!)
rule: En inglés la edad se dice con el verbo TO BE: I am 20 (years old). Nunca con 'have'.
I am · you are · he / she / it is · we are · they are.
Negativo: I am not · he is not (isn't) · they are not (aren't). Pregunta: Are you...? Is he...?

examples.en: I am 20 years old.
She is a technician.
We are students.

exercises.why: La edad se dice con 'am': I am 20.

title: Have / has
rule: Usamos HAVE con I, you, we, they. Usamos HAS con he, she, it.
I have a laptop. She has a laptop. The company has a server.
Pregunta: Do you have...? Does she have...? Negativo: I don't have... She doesn't have...

examples.en: She has a laptop with 16 GB of RAM.
examples.es: Ella tiene un portátil con 16 GB de RAM.

examples.en: We have two servers.

exercises.q: She ___ a laptop with 16 GB of RAM. (have)

title: Present simple: he / she / it + -s
rule: Con he, she, it el verbo añade -s: work → works.
Si acaba en s, sh, ch, x, o añade -es: fix → fixes, watch → watches, go → goes.
Si acaba en consonante + y cambia a -ies: study → studies. Have → has.

examples.en: He works in a big company.
examples.es: Él trabaja en una empresa grande.

examples.en: She studies Network Services.

exercises.q: My brother ___ to school by bus. (go)

title: Present simple: negativo y preguntas
rule: Negativo: do not (don't) / does not (doesn't) + verbo base. He doesn't work (no 'works').
Pregunta: Do / Does + sujeto + verbo base? Does she use a mouse?
Con does/doesn't el verbo NO lleva -s.

examples.en: She doesn't like Web Applications.
examples.es: No le gustan las Aplicaciones web.

examples.en: Does he work in Madrid?

exercises.a: Does she use an optical mouse?

exercises.q: What ___ he do? He is a technician. (do/does)

title: Artículos: a / an / the
rule: A se usa delante de un sonido de consonante: a laptop, a server.
AN delante de un sonido de vocal: an optical mouse, an IT technician (IT = /ai-ti/), an hour (la h es muda).
THE para algo concreto o ya conocido: Close the door.

examples.en: She is an IT technician.
He has an optical mouse.

exercises.why: hour: la h es muda → an.

title: There is / There are
rule: There is + singular: There is a server in the room.
There are + plural: There are two printers.
Negativo: There isn't a... / There aren't any... Pregunta: Is there a...? Are there any...?

examples.en: There is a switch in the server room.
examples.es: Hay un conmutador en la sala de servidores.

examples.en: There are two printers in the office.
examples.es: Hay dos impresoras en la oficina.

exercises.q: There ___ three computers on the desk. (is/are)
There ___ a problem with the cable. (is/are)
There ___ any viruses on this laptop.
___ there a printer? Yes, there is.

exercises.a: There is a switch in the server room

title: Can / must / should
rule: CAN = poder / saber. CAN'T = no poder.
MUST = obligación (hay que). MUSTN'T = prohibido.
SHOULD = consejo (deberías). Siempre + verbo base, sin 'to' ni -s.

examples.en: You must save your files.
You should back up your data.
examples.es: Deberías hacer copia de tus datos.

exercises.q: You ___ back up your files. It is a good idea.
Employees ___ share their passwords. It is forbidden.
You ___ wear an antistatic strap. It is a safety rule.
___ you help me with this computer?
You ___ unplug the cable before you open the case. (must / mustn't)

title: Comparativos (más ... que)
rule: Adjetivo corto: +er than → fast → faster than; cheap → cheaper.
Acaba en -e: +r → large → larger. Consonante+y → -ier → heavy → heavier. Una vocal + una consonante: se dobla → big → bigger.
Adjetivo largo (2+ sílabas): more + adjetivo + than → more convenient, more secure, more compact, more reliable.
Irregulares: good → better, bad → worse. Nunca 'more faster'.

examples.en: Flat panel monitors are brighter than CRT monitors.
examples.es: Los monitores planos son más brillantes que los CRT.

examples.en: Wi-Fi is more convenient than a cable.
examples.es: El wifi es más cómodo que un cable.

exercises.q: Modern flat panel monitors are (bright) ___ than old CRT monitors.
Modern flat panel monitors are (compact) ___ than old CRT monitors.
exercises.why: compact es largo para el examen → more compact.

exercises.q: An SSD is (fast) ___ than a hard disk drive.
This laptop is (heavy) ___ than that one.
This server is (good) ___ than the old one.
Wi-Fi is (convenient) ___ than a cable for mobile devices.
A desktop is (big) ___ than a laptop.
This network is ___ than that one.
The old monitor is (bad) ___ than the new one.
A tablet is (light) ___ than a laptop.
Cloud storage is (cheap) ___ than a new server.

title: Superlativos (el más ...)
rule: Adjetivo corto: the + adj + est → the fastest, the cheapest.
Adjetivo largo: the most + adj → the most convenient, the most important.
Irregulares: the best, the worst. Se usa 'the' siempre.

examples.en: This is the fastest computer in the office.
examples.es: Este es el ordenador más rápido de la oficina.

examples.en: Wireless is the most convenient method.
examples.es: Lo inalámbrico es el método más cómodo.

exercises.q: Using a wireless network is the (convenient) ___ method for mobile devices.
This is the (fast) ___ computer in the office.
A firewall is one of the (important) ___ security tools.
This is the (good) ___ laptop in the shop.
He is the (young) ___ technician in the team.
It is the (bad) ___ virus I have ever seen.
Fiber is the (fast) ___ type of connection.
This is ___ printer in the office.
It is the (big) ___ server room in the building.

title: La hora en inglés
rule: o'clock = en punto (ten o'clock). Past = y (half past ten, a quarter past eleven, twenty past four).
To = menos (a quarter to eleven = 10:45, twenty-five to ten = 9:35).
Half past = y media. a quarter = un cuarto (15 minutos).

examples.en: It is a quarter to eleven. (10:45)
It is twenty-five to ten. (9:35)

title: Direcciones y preposiciones de lugar
rule: Opposite = enfrente de. Next to = al lado de. Between = entre. Behind = detrás. In front of = delante.
Turn left / turn right = gire a la izquierda / derecha. Walk straight ahead = siga recto. Go down / go up = baje / suba.
Pedir educadamente: Excuse me, could you tell me how to get to...? / Would you mind telling me where... is?

examples.en: The boardroom is opposite the open-plan office.
examples.es: La sala de juntas está enfrente de la oficina diáfana.

examples.en: Turn right and walk straight ahead.
examples.es: Gire a la derecha y siga recto.

exercises.q: The boardroom is ___ the open-plan office. (enfrente)
The meeting room is ___ the director's office and the conference room. (entre)
Turn ___ at the end of the corridor. (a la izquierda)
Take the lift ___ to the first floor.
The IT office is ___ to the restrooms. (al lado)

title: Palabras interrogativas
rule: What = qué. Where = dónde. When = cuándo. Who = quién. Why = por qué (Because = porque). How = cómo. Which = cuál.
How old = qué edad. How much = cuánto (incontable / precio). How many = cuántos (contable).
Orden: palabra interrogativa + do/does/is/are + sujeto: Where do you live?

examples.en: How many ports does it have?
Why do you want this job?

exercises.q: ___ do you study English? Because I need it for work.
___ is the meeting? At ten o'clock.

title: Pasado simple
rule: Regulares: verbo + -ed → install → installed, replace → replaced.
Irregulares: go → went, have → had, buy → bought, break → broke, send → sent, forget → forgot, write → wrote.
Negativo y pregunta: did / didn't + verbo base: I didn't replace it. Did you finish?

examples.en: Yesterday I installed the update.
She went to the office by bus.
examples.es: Fue a la oficina en autobús.

exercises.q: She ___ to the office by bus. (go)

title: Voz pasiva
rule: Presente: is / are + participio → The server is updated every night.
Pasado: was / were + participio → The PC was assembled yesterday.
Se usa cuando importa más la acción que quién la hace. Con 'by' se dice quién: assembled by technicians.

examples.en: Passwords are changed every three months.
examples.es: Las contraseñas se cambian cada tres meses.

examples.en: The new PC was assembled yesterday.
examples.es: El PC nuevo se montó ayer.

exercises.q: The files ___ on the server. (store, pasiva)

title: Futuro: will y going to
rule: WILL: decisiones en el momento y promesas → I will restart it.
GOING TO: planes ya decididos → I am going to replace the cable. We are going to update the servers on Saturday.
Siempre + verbo base.

examples.en: I'm going to replace the cable.
I will help you.

exercises.q: I ___ buy a new laptop next month. (plan)
We ___ update the servers on Saturday.

title: Condicional 1 y oraciones de relativo
rule: If + presente, will + verbo base: If you restart the computer, it will work.
Who = personas. Which / that = cosas. Where = lugares.
A technician is a person who fixes computers. A router is a device which connects networks.

examples.en: If the server fails, the network will stop.
examples.es: Si el servidor falla, la red se parará.

examples.en: A technician is a person who fixes computers.
examples.es: Un técnico es una persona que arregla ordenadores.

exercises.q: If the server fails, the network ___ stop.
If you ___ your files, you will lose them. (not back up)
A technician is a person ___ fixes computers.
A router is a device ___ connects networks.
The office ___ I work is big.

title: Orden de la frase
rule: Orden básico: Sujeto + verbo + complemento + lugar + tiempo → I study English every day.
El adjetivo va ANTES del sustantivo: a new laptop (no 'a laptop new').
En preguntas: auxiliar + sujeto + verbo: Can you restart the computer?

examples.en: She works in a small company.
He has a new laptop.

exercises.a: She works in a small company

title: Presente simple o presente continuo
rule: PRESENTE SIMPLE = hábitos y hechos: always, every day, usually, never, in summer. I check the backups every day.
PRESENTE CONTINUO = ahora mismo: am / is / are + verbo-ing. I am updating the server now.
Palabras clave del continuo: now, right now, at the moment, today, this week. Pregunta: Are you watching TV now? / Do you always eat bread?
Verbos de estado (know, want, like, need, have = tener) casi nunca van en continuo: I know the answer (no 'I am knowing').

examples.en: I check the backups every day.
examples.es: Reviso las copias de seguridad todos los días.

examples.en: She is installing a program right now.
examples.es: Ella está instalando un programa ahora mismo.

exercises.q: He always ___ coffee in the morning. (drink)
___ you using the printer at the moment?

exercises.why: know es verbo de estado: no se usa en continuo.

exercises.q: My brother ___ in a big company every summer.

title: Pasado continuo: when y while
rule: PASADO CONTINUO: was / were + verbo-ing → acción en progreso en el pasado. I was reading in bed.
Negativo: wasn't / weren't + -ing. Pregunta: What were you doing at this time yesterday?
WHILE = mientras, dos acciones al mismo tiempo (las dos en continuo). We were watching the match while they were cooking.
WHEN = cuando, una acción corta interrumpe la larga: I was reading in bed when he arrived (arrived = pasado simple).

examples.en: I was reading in bed when you arrived.
examples.es: Estaba leyendo en la cama cuando llegaste.

examples.en: What were you doing at this time yesterday?
examples.es: ¿Qué estabas haciendo a esta hora ayer?

exercises.q: I ___ a cable when the lights went out.
We were watching the match ___ they were cooking. (when / while)
exercises.why: Dos acciones a la vez → while

exercises.q: What ___ you doing at this time yesterday? (be)
He ___ working when the server crashed.
They ___ updating the PCs when the boss came in. (be)

exercises.a: I was installing Windows when you called

exercises.q: While I ___ the laptop, she was answering emails.

title: Presente perfecto: have / has + participio
rule: Forma: have / has + participio. Regular: visited, finished. Irregular: eaten, done, been, written, gone.
Se usa para acciones que empezaron en el pasado y siguen, o cuyo efecto vemos ahora. NO se traduce siempre como en español.
Palabras clave: for (durante), since (desde), already (ya), yet (todavía, en negativas y preguntas), ever, never, just.
Sarah has lived in Madrid since 2006. = Sarah vive en Madrid desde 2006. I haven't finished yet.

examples.en: She has lived in Madrid since 2006.
You haven't finished your homework.

exercises.q: We ___ the server twice this week. (restart)
I have worked here ___ three years.
He ___ his homework. (do, ya lo ha hecho)

title: Pasado perfecto: had + participio
rule: Forma: had + participio (igual para todas las personas). I had finished.
Sitúa una acción en el pasado ANTES de otra acción pasada: I had already finished when you arrived.
Es imprescindible para el estilo indirecto (reported speech): She said she had restarted the server.

examples.en: I had already finished when you arrived.
He said he had lost his password.
examples.es: Dijo que había perdido su contraseña.

exercises.q: I ___ already finished when you arrived. (have)
When the technician arrived, the user ___ the PC.
exercises.why: Primero reinició; después llegó el técnico → had restarted

options: He had gone home before I called.
He has gone home before I called.
He had went home before I called.

title: Imperativos (órdenes y peticiones educadas)
rule: IMPERATIVO = verbo base sin sujeto: Restart the computer. Plug in the cable.
Negativo: Don't + verbo base: Don't unplug it. Don't touch the screen.
Más educado: Please + imperativo, o Could you / Would you / Can you + verbo base? Could you restart your computer, please?
Con un cliente es mejor ser educado: Please wait a moment. Could you tell me your name, please?

examples.en: Please restart your computer.
Don't unplug the cable.

exercises.q: ___ the power cable before you open the case.
___ touch the screen with wet hands.

exercises.why: Could you...? es la forma más educada.

exercises.a: Could you tell me your name please?

exercises.q: Cuando hablas con un cliente enfadado dices:
options: Please wait a moment. I will help you.
